component.name: Roxora Imager
component.summary: Write Roxora images to SD cards, USB drives and board storage

description.p: Roxora Imager writes Roxora images, Ubuntu with Armbian kernels for single-board computers, to SD cards and USB drives, and to a board's eMMC or SPI NOR flash over USB in Maskrom mode.
It downloads images from the Roxora releases on GitHub, checks them against the release checksums, and reads every write back to compare it with the release.
Images a release carries in parts may name them .001, .002 as well as .part1, .part2.

Simplified Chinese. Save an image as a file for Ventoy or a virtual machine. Downloads go on where they stopped. Maskrom: a vendor's update.img, a copy of the SPI flash before it is written, and a line that says whether a board is connected. A failed write offers Try again and Report a problem. Release tiers for the app's own updates, and native Windows on Arm packages.

Only the newest release is listed, older releases and betas are folded away. On Linux, built-in disks such as a board's eMMC or NVMe drive can be written once shown, and a copy installed from an apt repository is updated by apt.
Sort the images by release, Ubuntu version, desktop, kernel or size. A write that ends with an unexpected error no longer leaves the app thinking it is still writing.
When a board's loader cannot read back past a point over USB, the result says how much was verified instead of failing.
Writing an RK3576 board over USB works when its loader still runs from an earlier attempt.
Writing an RK3576 board over USB no longer stops after the loader. On macOS, updates install inside the app, through Homebrew or from the DMG. Copy buttons work.
Downloads Roxora's desktop images, which releases carry in parts, joining and checking them. Roxora's colours in the light and dark theme.
The first normal release. Checks for updates and installs them, lists Roxora's GNOME desktop images, chooses Ubuntu 26.04 by default, and reads beta releases.

Write an image file from this computer, such as one downloaded from the Roxora website. On macOS, drives are written through authopen with one password prompt and no Full Disk Access. Files that are not bootloaders are refused for SPI NOR flash when chosen.
Writing no longer stops with a "file closed" error after the data is written, before the drive is read back.
Writing an SD card or USB drive works again: the step that asks for administrator rights failed at once on every system.
